guided.prompt: The text has two title lines before the header. Replicate Source, Remove Top Rows (2), Promoted Headers and Changed Type for `Qty` (non-numbers become missing). Print the column names as a list, then the `Qty` values as a list, then the number of missing `Qty` values as an integer.
guided.starter:

import pandas as pd

text = "Monthly export
Generated by ERP
OrderID,Region,Qty
1, north ,4
2,South,n/a
3,NORTH,6
4,South,2

"

guided.solution:
import io
import pandas as pd

text = "Monthly export\nGenerated by ERP\nOrderID,Region,Qty\n1, north ,4\n2,South,n/a\n3,NORTH,6\n4,South,2\n4,South,2\n"

guided.title: Unpivot Other Columns
guided.prompt: The wide table has `Region`, `Jan`, `Feb`, `Mar`. Unpivot everything except `Region` into columns `Month` and `Amount`, and print the total `Amount` per `Month` in the order Jan, Feb, Mar as a dictionary.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd

wide = pd.DataFrame({"Region": ["North", "South", "East"], "Jan": [10, 20, 30], "Feb": [15, 25, 35], "Mar": [20, 30, 40]})
# unpivot, then total by Month
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd

wide = pd.DataFrame({"Region": ["North", "South", "East"], "Jan": [10, 20, 30], "Feb": [15, 25, 35], "Mar": [20, 30, 40]})
long = wide.melt(id_vars="Region", var_name="Month", value_name="Amount")
print(long.groupby("Month", sort=False)["Amount"].sum().to_dict())

guided.title: Write the step list (written)
guided.prompt: A CSV export has a title line, a header, region names with stray spaces in mixed case, a Qty column containing `n/a` and a footer line `Total,,`. Write the Power Query steps, in order, that import and clean it ready for a PivotTable, say where in Excel you start, and explain what happens at the next Refresh.
guided.solution: Start with Data, Get Data, From File, From Text/CSV, pick the file, and choose Transform Data. Steps: (1) Source; (2) Remove Top Rows (1) to drop the title line; (3) Use First Row as Headers; (4) Remove Bottom Rows (1) to remove the `Total` footer; (5) Changed Type: Region text, Qty whole number, so `n/a` becomes Error; (6) Remove Errors on Qty (or Replace Errors, after looking at the rows); (7) Trim and Capitalize Each Word on Region; (8) Remove Duplicates. Finally Home, Close & Load to a Table on a new sheet. At the next Refresh Power Query reads the new file and runs the same steps in order; the source file is never altered and manual edits of the loaded Table are overwritten.
hints: Remove Top Rows comes before promoting the header.
Clean and trim text before removing duplicates.
Refresh re-runs all steps on the current source.
rubric: Remove Top Rows comes before Use First Row as Headers.
The footer is removed and the types are set.
Trim and case changes come before Remove Duplicates.
Explains that Refresh re-runs the steps and the source is unchanged.

jan = "Export\nRegion,Qty\n north ,3\nNorth,3\nTest,9\nSouth,x\nSouth,5\n"
feb = jan + "East,7\nsouth ,1\n"

independent.solution:
import io
import pandas as pd

jan = "Export\nRegion,Qty\n north ,3\nNorth,3\nTest,9\nSouth,x\nSouth,5\n"
feb = jan + "East,7\nsouth ,1\n"

def query(text):
    df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(text), skiprows=1)
    df["Qty"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Qty"], errors="coerce")
    df["Region"] = df["Region"].str.strip().str.title()
    df = df.dropna(subset=["Qty"]).drop_duplicates()
    return df[df["Region"] != "Test"].reset_index(drop=True)

print(query(jan).to_string(index=False))
print(float(query(feb)["Qty"].sum()))

independent.title: Unpivot, clean and summarise
independent.prompt: The wide table has messy region names and months as columns. Trim and capitalise `Region`, unpivot the month columns to `Month` and `Amount`, drop rows where `Amount` is missing, then print the total `Amount` per `Region` as a Series with `to_string()`, sorted by Region.
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd

wide = pd.DataFrame({"Region": [" north", "SOUTH ", "North"], "Jan": [10, 20, 5], "Feb": [15, None, 7], "Mar": [20, 30, None]})
# clean, unpivot, drop missing, total per Region
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd

wide = pd.DataFrame({"Region": [" north", "SOUTH ", "North"], "Jan": [10, 20, 5], "Feb": [15, None, 7], "Mar": [20, 30, None]})
wide["Region"] = wide["Region"].str.strip().str.title()
long = wide.melt(id_vars="Region", var_name="Month", value_name="Amount").dropna(subset=["Amount"])
print(long.groupby("Region")["Amount"].sum().to_string())

independent.title: Fix a broken refresh (written, stretch)
independent.prompt: After next month's file arrives, the query shows an error 'The column Mar of the table wasn't found' and a manager reports that April is missing from the totals. Explain the likely causes in the Applied Steps (an unpivot of selected columns, a renamed column in the source, a Changed Type step that names columns), and how you would fix each and prevent them.
independent.solution: The Changed Type step is a recorded step that names each column, so if the source no longer has `Mar` (it was renamed or dropped) the step fails. Open the failing step in Applied Steps, adjust or delete it, and reapply the type once on the columns that really exist. The missing April total comes from an Unpivot Columns step that selected only Jan, Feb and Mar: new month columns are left wide and not unpivoted. Replace it with Unpivot Other Columns on the identifier column, so that any new month column is unpivoted at the next Refresh. To prevent both problems, keep the identifier columns explicit, avoid steps that name many value columns, and compare the loaded Table's total with the source total after every refresh.
rubric: Identifies the Changed Type step naming a missing column.
Identifies Unpivot of selected columns versus Unpivot Other Columns.
Gives a reconciliation check after refresh.

environment.note: Power Query is in Excel for Windows 2016 or later and Microsoft 365 (Data tab, Get Data), and in Microsoft 365 for Mac with fewer connectors; Excel 2010 and 2013 need the Power Query add-in, and LibreOffice Calc has no Power Query. The ribbon names can vary slightly between versions. The graded exercises replicate the steps with pandas, which runs in the browser.

checks.question: What happens to the source CSV file when you load a Power Query result?
options: It is modified with the cleaned data
It is not changed; the query reads it and writes a separate Table
checks.explanation: Power Query only reads the source. The cleaned data is loaded into a Table or the Data Model, so the original stays as it was.

checks.question: Region values are ` north`, `North` and `NORTH `. Which step order leaves one row after Remove Duplicates?
options: Remove Duplicates, then Trim and Capitalize
Trim and Capitalize, then Remove Duplicates
checks.explanation: Remove Duplicates compares values exactly, case included. The values must first be trimmed and given the same case; otherwise all three rows survive.

checks.question: A Qty column contains the text n/a. After Changed Type to whole number, what happens?
options: The query stops with a message
That cell shows Error and the query continues
checks.explanation: Values that cannot be converted become Error cells. They are not removed or replaced with 0 automatically, so use Remove Errors or Replace Errors on purpose.

checks.question: You filter Region to `north` in Power Query, but the data holds `North`. What is the result?
checks.explanation: Power Query text filters are case-sensitive, unlike worksheet SUMIFS. Fix the case with a transform step first.

checks.question: Why is Unpivot Other Columns safer than unpivoting the selected month columns?
options: New month columns are unpivoted automatically on refresh
checks.explanation: Unpivot Other Columns names the identifier columns and unpivots everything else, so a new column such as Apr is included next time. Unpivoting selected columns leaves new columns wide.
